_source: Ella Mobile's Word of the day words (supabase/functions/ella/words.ts, WORD_LISTS, as of 5fafec3), word for word: three lists of fifteen, each for the levels it names. Each word has what Ella says it means, her own example of it in use, its three questions in the order she asks them (the last for a sentence of their own), each with an answer to follow for a learner who does not know what to say, and any other ways it is written or said. Read by the Rust backend (src-tauri/src/words.rs).

words.meaning: Happy means you feel good, and you want to smile.
words.example: The baby is happy with her new toy.

questions.example: Music makes me happy.
I am happy on Sundays.
My mother is happy today.

words.meaning: Hungry means your stomach is empty, and you want to eat.
words.example: The children are hungry after playing cricket.

questions.example: I am hungry in the morning.

questions.ask: What do you eat when you are hungry?
questions.example: When I am hungry, I eat roti.
My little brother is always hungry.

words.meaning: Tired means your body wants to rest or sleep.
words.example: The players are tired after the long match.

questions.example: I feel tired at night.

questions.ask: What do you do when you are tired?
questions.example: When I am tired, I sleep.
My father is tired after work.

words.meaning: Favourite means you like it more than all the others.
words.example: Sunday is my favourite day of the week.

questions.example: My favourite food is biryani.
My favourite colour is blue.
Cricket is my favourite game.

words.meaning: Busy means you have a lot of work and no free time.
words.example: The doctor is busy, so please wait.

questions.example: I am busy in the morning.

questions.ask: Who is busy in your family?
questions.example: My mother is always busy.
The market is busy on Sunday.

words.meaning: Early means before the usual time, the opposite of late.
words.example: The bus came early today.

questions.example: Yes, I get up early.

questions.ask: What do you do early in the morning?
questions.example: Early in the morning, I drink tea.
I go to bed early.

words.meaning: Cold means not warm, like ice or a winter morning.
words.example: In December, Delhi is very cold.

questions.example: I feel cold in the morning.

questions.ask: What do you drink when it is cold?
questions.example: I drink hot tea when it is cold.
The water is very cold.

words.meaning: Cook means make food hot and ready to eat.
words.example: On Sundays, we cook dinner together.

questions.example: My mother cooks in my home.
I can cook rice and dal.
I cook eggs on Sunday.

words.meaning: Clean means not dirty. When you clean, you wash or wipe something.
words.example: We clean the whole house before Diwali.

questions.ask: What do you clean at home?
questions.example: I clean my room.
Yes, my street is clean.
My hands are clean.

words.meaning: Noisy means full of loud sounds, the opposite of quiet.
words.example: The wedding band is very noisy.

questions.ask: What place near you is noisy?
questions.example: The market is noisy.

questions.ask: Is your home noisy or quiet?
questions.example: My home is noisy in the evening.
The bus is very noisy.

words.meaning: Healthy means good for your body, or strong and not sick.
words.example: The new baby is strong and healthy.

questions.example: Fruit and dal are healthy.

questions.ask: What do you do to stay healthy?
questions.example: I walk every day to stay healthy.
My grandfather is very healthy.

words.meaning: Help means do something for someone, so their work is easier.
words.example: Good friends always help each other.

questions.example: I help my mother at home.
My teacher helps me with English.
I help my friend with maths.

words.meaning: Delicious means very tasty, so you want to eat more.
words.example: The biryani at the party was delicious.

questions.example: Mangoes are delicious.
Grandma makes delicious food.
This samosa is delicious.

words.meaning: Careful means you take care, so nothing bad happens.
words.example: Be careful, the floor is wet.

questions.ask: When do you need to be careful?
questions.example: I am careful on the road.

questions.ask: Are you careful with your phone?
questions.example: Yes, I am careful with my phone.
Be careful with hot tea.

words.meaning: Late means after the right time, the opposite of early.
words.example: I missed the bus because I was late.

questions.example: My brother is often late.

questions.ask: What do you do when you are late?
questions.example: When I am late, I run.
The train is late today.

words.meaning: Brave means you do something hard or scary, even when you feel afraid.
words.example: My little brother was brave when he got his injection.

questions.example: I was brave at the dentist.

questions.ask: Who is the bravest person you know?
questions.example: My grandmother is very brave.
My friend was brave on stage.

words.meaning: Patient means you can wait calmly, without getting angry or upset.
words.example: My grandfather is patient when he teaches me chess.

questions.example: Yes, I am patient with children.

questions.ask: When is it hard to be patient?
questions.example: It is hard to be patient in traffic.
My teacher is very patient.

words.meaning: Crowded means full of people, with very little space to move.
words.example: The local train is crowded in the morning.

questions.ask: Which place near you is crowded?
questions.example: The market near me is always crowded.

questions.ask: How do you feel in crowded places?
questions.example: I feel tired in crowded places.
The bus was crowded today.

words.meaning: Celebrate means do something special and happy for a festival or good news.
words.example: Everyone celebrated when India won the match.

questions.example: We celebrate Diwali with sweets.

questions.ask: How do you celebrate your birthday?
questions.example: I celebrate my birthday with cake.
We celebrated my sister's wedding.

words.meaning: Borrow means take something from someone for a short time, then give it back.
words.example: I borrowed a book from the library.

questions.example: I often borrow my sister's charger.

questions.ask: Is it okay to borrow money?
questions.example: No, I don't like to borrow money.
Can I borrow your pen?

words.meaning: Proud means you feel happy about something good you or your family did.
words.example: The whole village was proud of the young doctor.

questions.example: I was proud when I passed my exam.
I am proud of my little sister.
My parents are proud of me.

words.meaning: Nervous means a bit worried or scared about something that will happen soon.
words.example: He was nervous before his job interview.

questions.example: I feel nervous before exams.

questions.ask: What do you do when you're nervous?
questions.example: I take a deep breath when I'm nervous.
I was nervous on my first day.

words.meaning: Comfortable means you feel relaxed, with no pain and no worry.
words.example: These old shoes are still very comfortable.

questions.example: I am comfortable at home.
Cotton clothes are very comfortable.
This chair is very comfortable.

words.meaning: Improve means get better, or make something better than before.
words.example: My cooking has improved a lot this year.

questions.ask: What do you want to improve?
questions.example: I want to improve my English.
Better roads would improve my town.
I practise every day to improve.

words.meaning: Decide means choose one thing after you think about it.
words.example: We decided to go to Goa for the holidays.

questions.example: I decided to wear my blue shirt.

questions.ask: Who decides what you eat at home?
questions.example: My mother decides what we eat.
I can't decide what to watch.

words.meaning: Expensive means it costs a lot of money, the opposite of cheap.
words.example: A taxi is more expensive than the metro.

questions.ask: What is expensive in your city?
questions.example: Houses are very expensive in my city.

questions.ask: What expensive thing do you want?
questions.example: I want an expensive watch.
Mangoes are expensive this year.

words.meaning: A habit is something you do again and again, often without thinking.
words.example: Biting your nails is a bad habit.

questions.example: My best habit is reading at night.

questions.ask: What habit do you want to stop?
questions.example: I want to stop my phone habit.
Walking is a good habit.

words.meaning: A surprise is something you did not expect, like a gift or sudden news.
words.example: My uncle's visit from Dubai was a big surprise.

questions.example: Yes, I love surprises.
A surprise party from my friends.
The news was a big surprise.

words.meaning: Advice is what someone tells you, to help you decide what to do.
words.example: The doctor gave me advice about my diet.

questions.example: My uncle gives me good advice.

questions.ask: What advice can you give a child?
questions.example: My advice is to read every day.
Thank you for your advice.

words.meaning: Confident means you believe you can do something well.
words.example: After weeks of practice, he felt confident about driving.

questions.example: I feel confident when I play football.
Practice makes a person confident.
I am confident about my exam.

words.meaning: Resilient means you recover quickly from hard times and keep going.
words.example: The resilient farmers planted again after the flood.

questions.ask: Who is resilient in your family?
questions.example: My grandfather is truly resilient.
Hard times make people resilient.

questions.ask: Say how you have been resilient.
questions.example: I was resilient after failing an exam.

words.meaning: Nostalgic means you think of happy times in the past, and miss them.
words.example: The smell of rain makes Grandma nostalgic for her village.

questions.example: Old Hindi songs make me nostalgic.

questions.ask: What do you feel nostalgic about?
questions.example: I'm nostalgic about school holidays.
Old photos always make me nostalgic.

words.meaning: Meticulous means very careful about every small detail, so nothing is wrong.
words.example: A meticulous tailor measures twice before cutting.

questions.example: Yes, I'm meticulous about my notes.
Surgeons need to be meticulous.
My sister plans trips meticulously.

words.meaning: Persuade means give good reasons so someone agrees or does what you ask.
words.example: She persuaded her parents to let her study abroad.

questions.example: My father is hard to persuade.

questions.ask: How do you persuade a friend?
questions.example: I persuade friends with good reasons.
I persuaded my dad to come.

words.meaning: Compromise means each side gives up a little, so both can agree.
words.example: My brother and I compromised and took turns with the TV.

questions.example: Yes, I often compromise.
Yes, every friendship needs compromise.
We made a compromise.

words.meaning: Ambitious means you want big success and work hard for it.
words.example: She is ambitious and wants to start her own company.

questions.example: Yes, I'm ambitious about my career.

questions.ask: Who is ambitious in your family?
questions.example: My cousin is very ambitious.
That's an ambitious plan for one week.

words.meaning: Procrastinate means keep putting off work you should do now.
words.example: I procrastinated and studied only the night before the exam.

questions.example: Yes, I procrastinate on cleaning.
We procrastinate on boring work.
Don't procrastinate on your homework.

words.meaning: Inevitable means sure to happen, and no one can stop it.
words.example: With so much traffic, being a little late was inevitable.

questions.example: Yes, change is inevitable in life.
Some mistakes are inevitable at first.
Monsoon delays are inevitable.

words.meaning: Empathy means you understand and share how another person feels.
words.example: Her empathy helped her friend through a hard time.

questions.example: My teacher shows me empathy.

questions.ask: Why is empathy important at work?
questions.example: Empathy helps a team work well.
Good doctors listen with empathy.

words.meaning: Versatile means able to do many things well, or be used in many ways.
words.example: A versatile actor can play a hero or a villain.

questions.example: Yes, I'm versatile at work.

questions.ask: What is versatile in your kitchen?
questions.example: A pressure cooker is very versatile.
Rice is a versatile food.

words.meaning: Candid means honest and direct, saying what you really think.
words.example: My coach gave me candid advice about my weak points.

questions.example: My best friend is always candid.
Yes, I like candid feedback at work.
Thank you for your candid answer.

words.meaning: Thrive means grow strong and do very well, because the conditions are right.
words.example: Children thrive when they feel loved and safe.

questions.example: I thrive in a busy team.

questions.ask: What do plants need to thrive?
questions.example: Plants need sun and water to thrive.
Small businesses thrive in my area.

words.meaning: A setback is a problem that stops your progress for a while.
words.example: The injury was a setback, but he soon played again.

questions.ask: How do you handle a setback?
questions.example: After a setback, I make a new plan.
Failing my driving test was a setback.
The rain was a big setback.

words.meaning: Perspective means the way you see and think about something.
words.example: Living in a village gave me a new perspective on life.

questions.example: Yes, travel changed my perspective.
New perspectives help me grow.
From my perspective, it's fine.

words.meaning: Hectic means very busy and rushed, with no time to rest.
words.example: Mornings are hectic when everyone needs the bathroom at once.

questions.example: Yes, today was very hectic.

questions.ask: How do you relax after a hectic day?
questions.example: After a hectic day, I listen to music.
Wedding season is always hectic.
